title: Rewrite instrumentation adapters to zero-allocation logging and slim trace forwarder
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
We will replace legacy instrumentation shims and the current logging path with a low-allocation, structured logging adapter and a slim OpenTelemetry trace forwarder. The goal is to reduce CPU/heap allocations during high QPS, lower p99 tail latency on the runtime, and simplify exporter semantics so downstream telemetry ingest costs drop.

Motivation:
- Current log pipeline uses string concatenation and an older logging library with expensive fmt-style formatting. This allocates per-request and shows up in flame graphs under high batching.
- The trace exporter currently builds heavy map structures and performs synchronous JSON marshaling on hot paths.
- Observed regression: +22% CPU at peak and 18% higher allocation rate in serving runtime compared to baseline after recent batching changes.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Introduce a zap-based structured logger shim with lazy field serialization and buffer pooling.
- Replace the heavy trace exporter with a lightweight forwarder that streams OTLP protobufs using a pooled encoder and avoids temporary map allocations.
- Provide a compatibility adapter so existing instrumentation calls (trace/log helpers) keep the same surface while being routed to the new implementations.
- Add end-to-end benchmarks and heatmaps into the console metric dashboard for runtime-telemetry cost across routes.
- Update SDK docs and provide migration notes for third-party repos that import internal logging helpers.

Design notes / Trade-offs:
- We keep the public helper APIs stable to avoid wide churn; this means adapter layer will perform minimal translation but keep zero-copy where possible.
- Zap was chosen for its performance and structured field APIs; we will vendor only the minimal subset to avoid dependency creep.
- We will not replace OTLP exporters entirely — instead we provide a slim forwarder that batches and encodes protobufs efficiently and hands them to the existing OTLP pipeline asynchronously. A follow-up can fully replace the pipeline if needed.

Testing and Metrics:
- Microbenchmarks: allocs/op, ns/op for log+trace hotpath (target: -40% allocs/op, -12% ns/op).
- Integration: run internal load harness (scale test) comparing baseline vs branch with 10k RPS traffic for typical request size. Measure CPU, heap, p99 latency, telemetry ingestion bytes.
- Observability: add dashboard tiles for "telemetry CPU", "telemetry allocs/sec", and per-route telemetry cost.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch with unit tests + microbenchmarks.
2) Canary deploy to non-critical internal cluster (redwood-canary-2) with traffic shadowing.
3) Gradual traffic ramp to 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, monitoring telemetry metrics and error rates.
4) If we see >5% regression in request latency or >3% error rate change, automatic rollback.

Backout / Rollback:
- Adapters are feature-flagged via runtime config. Immediate rollout failure handled by flipping the flag to revert to legacy path.

Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: subtle semantic differences in field ordering or error formatting. Mitigation: compatibility tests comparing wire-level logs and traces between legacy and new adapter for sample traces.
- Risk: dependency transitive upgrade could bump runtime linking. Mitigation: vendor minimal zap subset and run plumbing smoke tests on Dedicated & Private clusters.

Open questions:
- Do we allow customers to opt into full zero-copy OTLP pipeline or keep forwarder as default? (product).
- Are there any remaining services that use the internal string-format logging helpers directly? We will scan repos and create small follow-up tickets for hand edits.

Deliverables / Acceptance criteria:
- New adapter merged and feature-flagged behind runtime flag "telemetry.v2.enabled".
- Microbenchmarks demonstrating at least 30% reduction in allocs/op and 8% p99 latency improvement for the hot path.
- No increase in customer-facing errors after 72h of 100% rollout on staging.
- Console dashboard reflecting telemetry cost savings and per-route breakdown.
